headline: TECTONIC METALS DRILLS 5.09 g/t Au OVER 21.34m AT BLACK CREEK — SECOND GOLD CENTRE EMERGING AT FLAT PROJECT, ALASKA
snippet: Tectonic Metals (TSXV: TECT) confirmed a second consecutive season of high-grade gold at Black Creek with hole CMR26-152 returning 5.09 g/t Au over 21.34m (including 17.34 g/t over 6.10m), and CMR26-153 hitting 1.89 g/t over 57.91m with a 6.31 g/t core over 7.62m. The results strengthen the case that Black Creek — situated 6km northeast of the main Chicken Mountain bulk-tonnage heap-leach target — is emerging as a distinct second intrusive gold centre, with the system still open in all directions.

headline: NEXGOLD HITS 84.30 g/t Au AT GOLDLUND ZONE 4 — EXPANDS ONTARIO DRILL PROGRAM BY 10,000m TO 35,000m ON STRENGTH OF RESULTS
snippet: NexGold Mining (TSXV: NEXG) reported 11 holes from Zone 4 at the Goldlund Deposit in Ontario, with intercepts including 3.08 g/t Au over 17.0m, 4.80 g/t over 5.6m, and a high-grade kicker of 84.30 g/t over 1.0m — extending mineralization adjacent to prior holes that returned 7.59 g/t over 9.0m. The company elected to expand its drill program from 25,000 to 35,000 metres based on the results, a direct confidence signal that the Goliath Gold Complex resource upgrade thesis is holding up hole after hole.

headline: COMEX COPPER SETS ALL-TIME RECORD $6.7270/LB — TARIFF ARBITRAGE PULLING GLOBAL SUPPLY INTO U.S. WAREHOUSES AHEAD OF POTENTIAL DUTIES
snippet: Comex copper hit a new all-time high of $6.7270 per pound on August 25, topping the previous record of $6.7140 set on August 12, as the US tariff threat continues to pull metal away from LME-stored supply and into American warehouses. Comex copper is now up 19% year-to-date and roughly 50% over the past year — meaning junior copper developers who dismissed the rally as speculative in early 2025 are now watching their optionality rebuild at a pace few consensus models predicted.

headline: GOLD HART COPPER MAPS MULTI-ZONE GOLD-COPPER-SILVER TARGETS AT NESSA COMPLEX — FIRST-EVER SURVEY IN CHILE'S DOMEYKO FAULT SYSTEM
snippet: Gold Hart Copper Corp. completed the first-ever comprehensive geochemical soil survey across its Nessa Complex properties in Chile's Domeyko Fault System, identifying multiple zones of anomalous gold, copper, silver, and associated pathfinder elements across the project footprint on August 24. The Domeyko is one of Chile's most prolific porphyry-hosting structural corridors; the survey delineates priority drill targets for what the company describes as its first systematic drill campaign at the property.

headline: ICG SILVER & GOLD ADVANCES TUSCARORA PHASE 1 TO 2,525m — FOUR NEVADA TARGETS DRILLED, ASSAYS PENDING AT BATTLE MOUNTAIN AND KING'S VEIN
snippet: ICG Silver & Gold announced August 25 that 2,525 metres have been drilled across 10 RC holes — 84% of the planned 3,000m Phase 1 program — at four targets in Nevada's Tuscarora District: Silica, Battle Mountain, King's Vein, and East Pediment. Preliminary geological logging confirms the intended geological horizons were encountered at each target; initial assay results from the first holes are pending with two additional holes planned to complete East Pediment.

headline: $419M RETAIL INFLOWS HIT GDX IN AUGUST — GOLD MINER ETF TRACKS TOWARD STRONGEST MONTHLY INTAKE SINCE FEBRUARY AS MINERS REBOUND
snippet: VanEck's GDX gold miner ETF attracted $419 million in retail inflows during August 2026, tracking toward its strongest monthly intake since February, as GDX posted a +21% gain during the week gold surged 7.2% to $4,710. The surge follows a notable dislocation where Agnico Eagle, Alamos, Equinox, and Coeur Mining all fell 6-10% while gold itself was climbing — and analysts now point to GDX's free cash flow/EV yield at record highs and forward P/E at a five-year low as the conditions that historically precede a miner re-rating cycle.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER HAVE ADDED $5 TRILLION IN COMBINED VALUE IN 2026 — THE FOUR MACRO FORCES BEHIND THE MOST SYNCHRONIZED METALS RALLY SINCE 1980
snippet: GoldSeek's latest macro analysis quantifies the 2026 precious metals rally: gold and silver together have added approximately $5 trillion in combined market value — a magnitude not seen since the synchronized commodity cycle of 1980. The piece identifies four converging forces: central bank reserve diversification away from US Treasuries, the dollar debasement trade triggered by Treasury's bond buyback expansion, industrial silver demand from electrification buildout, and a generational shift in retail investor behaviour toward hard assets after years of inflation erosion. The $5 trillion figure provides context for why institutional capital is treating this rally differently from 2019–2020's QE-driven run.

headline: UBS: HOLD GOLD EVEN AS LONG-TERM YIELDS RISE — TREASURY BUYBACK BREAKS THE USUAL RATE/GOLD INVERSE RELATIONSHIP
snippet: UBS published guidance for institutional clients to maintain strategic gold allocations even as long-end US Treasury yields rise — a dynamic that would normally be bearish for gold. The bank argues Treasury's bond buyback program has broken the conventional inverse relationship between real yields and gold: when 10- and 30-year yields rise because the government is simultaneously buying and expanding the monetary base to fund buybacks, gold's role as a currency substitute strengthens rather than weakens. UBS models a 5-7% strategic gold allocation as the optimal hedge in this fiscal-credibility-risk environment.

headline: ABCOURT MINES (ABI) TRANSITIONS TO LONG-HOLE STOPING — UNDERGROUND ACCELERATION TARGETS HIGHER GRADE AND LARGER TONNAGE IN H2 2026
snippet: Abcourt Mines (TSXV: ABI) reported July 2026 operational results and announced a strategic transition from cut-and-fill to long-hole stoping at its underground operation — a method change designed to increase ore tonnage per blast while targeting higher-grade stope panels in the mine plan's second half. The company framed the transition as a key step toward optimized production and an improved cost structure heading into H2 2026.

headline: GAO FLAGS $140B U.S. URANIUM ENRICHMENT PROGRAM HAS NO COST REPORTING TO CONGRESS — OVERSIGHT GAP IN AMERICA'S NUCLEAR FUEL BUILDUP
snippet: The American Nuclear Society's Nuclear Newswire reported August 25 on a new GAO report (GAO-26-107385) finding that the National Nuclear Security Administration is pursuing three long-term uranium enrichment efforts projected to cost $140 billion through 2105 — yet has failed to report these costs to Congress as legally required. The DOE's civilian enrichment expansion also lacks an economic analysis, strategic plan, or cost estimates. For uranium investors, the GAO finding is double-edged: it confirms the U.S. domestic enrichment buildout is real and funded, but the execution oversight gaps introduce schedule risk for the $3.7 billion IRA nuclear fuel package currently working through the system.
